title: Introduction to eegwhiten
text: eegwhiten provides covariance whitening covariance-based transfer-learning tools EEG multichannel signals. core model-based fit/transform workflow: Rows trials/epochs/samples; columns channels/features. Fit training data, apply new data. Six whitening methods, covariance shrinkage, robust estimators, dimensionality reduction, cross-validated tuning. top whitening adds pieces needed cross-session / cross-subject work: Euclidean alignment per-domain recentering, Riemannian tangent-space mapping, generalized-eigenvalue (“relative”) whitening.
code: library(eegwhiten)

title: Introduction to eegwhiten
code: X_train <- matrix(rnorm(300 * 16), 300, 16) X_test  <- matrix(rnorm(120 * 16), 120, 16) colnames(X_train) <- paste0("Ch", 1:16) colnames(X_test)  <- colnames(X_train)  m <- whiten_model(X_train, method = "PCA", var_threshold = 0.95, lambda = "auto") print(m) #> <whiten_model> #>   method      : PCA  #>   dimensions  : 16 -> 16  #>   n_comp      : 16  #>   var_threshold: 0.95  #>   explained_var: 1  #>   lambda      : 1  #>   shrink_target: identity  #>   eig_method  : auto  #>   fast_mode   : FALSE  #>   cov_estimator: empirical  #>   weighted_fit: FALSE  #>   n_obs       : 300  #>   updates     : 0  #>   lambda_mode :auto (oas)  Z_test <- predict(m, X_test) dim(Z_test) #> [1] 120  16  # Inverse transform (note: model-first argument order) X_rec <- unwhiten(m, Z_test) dim(X_rec) #> [1] 120  16

title: Introduction to eegwhiten
text: Independent per-matrix whitening removes -session covariance structure transfer learning needs. eegwhiten offers alignment instead. Per-domain recentering (recenter()) aligns session covariance, mapping every domain identity – Euclidean Alignment idea Wu (2019): Across several drifting sessions, recentering collapses -session Riemannian distances toward zero:  Euclidean alignment (euclidean_alignment()) instead builds one shared transform grand-mean covariance: predict time, self_center = TRUE centers test data mean, helps test session drifted relative training:
code: X_list <- list(   matrix(rnorm(200 * 8), 200, 8),   matrix(rnorm(180 * 8), 180, 8) %*% diag(1:8)  # a shifted session )  out <- whiten_batch(X_list, mode = "recenter") round(diag(cov(out[[2]]$Z)), 3)   # each domain -> identity #> [1] 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 sessions <- lapply(1:6, function(s) {   S <- crossprod(matrix(rnorm(64), 8, 8)) + diag(8)   matrix(rnorm(200 * 8), 200, 8) %*% chol(S * runif(1, 0.5, 2)) }) pair_d <- function(cl) {   d <- c(); k <- length(cl)   for (i in 1:(k - 1)) for (j in (i + 1):k) d <- c(d, riemann_distance(cl[[i]], cl[[j]]))   d } raw <- pair_d(lapply(sessions, cov)) rc  <- pair_d(lapply(whiten_batch(sessions, mode = "recenter"), function(o) cov(o$Z))) boxplot(list(raw = raw, recentered = rc), ylab = "pairwise Riemannian distance",         col = c("#FDDBC7", "#2166AC"), main = "between-session distance") ea <- euclidean_alignment(X_list, input = "raw", mean_method = "logeuclid") str(ea$aligned, max.level = 1) #> List of 2 #>  $ : num [1:200, 1:8] -1.196 -0.572 0.591 1.129 0.689 ... #>  $ : num [1:180, 1:8] 0.566 -1.6467 1.492 -0.0236 -1.0221 ... m_tr <- whiten_model(X_list[[1]], method = "ZCA", lambda = 0.1) Z_drift <- predict(m_tr, X_list[[2]], self_center = TRUE) dim(Z_drift) #> [1] 180   8

title: eegwhiten 1.0.0
text: First stable release. public API now considered stable: six whitening transforms, whiten_model() fit/predict() workflow (including dimension reduction, shrinkage, robust covariance estimators), covariance-alignment tools (Euclidean alignment, recentering, barycenter whitening), Riemannian tangent-space helpers, diagnostics/reporting functions. breaking changes 0.5.2; release marks transition experimental lifecycle.

title: eegwhiten 0.5.2
text: Added gallery demonstration figures README pkgdown site (whitening /, six transforms, tangent-space alignment, covariance-estimator comparisons), plus live illustrations vignette. figures reproducible tools/make-figures.R.

title: eegwhiten 0.5.1
text: whiten_batch(mode = "ea", center = TRUE) now reports per-matrix centering vector actually subtracted (column means) instead zero vector, reconstructing (Z, W, center) recovers original data. euclidean_alignment() now returns vectors centers list. model fitted lambda = "auto" shrink_target = "diagonal" now reports lambda_method = "ss" (Schaefer-Strimmer, estimator actually used) instead ignored "oas"/"lw" input, object print() / summary().

title: eegwhiten 0.5.0
text: riemann_distance() spd_mean() expose affine-invariant Riemannian (log-Euclidean / Euclidean) distance mean SPD covariance matrices. barycenter_whitener() fits whitener maps geometric mean set covariances identity (align Riemannian barycenter). lambda = "auto" now works shrink_target = "diagonal", using scale-invariant Schaefer-Strimmer shrinkage intensity (verified corpcor::estimate.lambda). epoch_covariances() accepts lambda = "auto" per-epoch Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage intensity.

title: eegwhiten 0.4.1
text: predict() now works directly auto_tune_whitening() result, applying selected best model. scale-invariant positive-definiteness fix now also covers whiten_fit() standalone ZCA_cor() / PCA_cor() functions (correlation-based methods check correlation matrix), relative tolerance single named constant. introductory vignette now covers alignment, Riemannian tangent-space, relative-whitening, shrinkage-target, online-update features. Refreshed package description; removed dead internal helpers.

title: eegwhiten 0.4.0
text: cov_estimator = "tyler" now restores covariance scale (Tyler’s iteration estimates trace-normalized shape), whitening produces approximately unit-variance data instead decorrelated--mis-scaled data. positive-definiteness check now scale-invariant (relative largest eigenvalue), well-conditioned data magnitude – e.g. EEG volts – longer falsely rejected. Correlation-based methods test positive-definiteness correlation matrix.

title: eegwhiten 0.4.0
text: Functions taking model data now use consistent model-first argument order: unwhiten(model, Z), unwhiten_fast(model, Z), unwhiten_tensor(model, Z_tensor), inverse_ea(model, Z). old data-first order still works deprecation warning. epoch_covariances() shrinkage argument renamed lambda (matching rest package); shrinkage deprecated. predict.whiten_model() argument recenter renamed self_center avoid clashing recenter() function; recenter deprecated. recenter(), whiten_relative(), tuning result (whiten_tune), ea_model now print() methods (predict() applicable), instead returning bare lists.

title: eegwhiten 0.4.0
text: Added pkgdown configuration, coverage workflow, R-devel/oldrel CI, CITATION, README badges, cran-comments.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md.

title: eegwhiten 0.3.0
text: Riemannian tangent space mapping. tangent_space() untangent_space() project SPD covariance matrices /tangent space reference mean (Riemann / log-Euclidean / Euclidean), isometric vectorization. epoch_covariances() builds per-trial covariances EEG tensor input. Per-domain recentering. recenter() aligns matrix covariance (true Euclidean Alignment semantics), whiten_batch() gains mode = "recenter". predict.whiten_model() gains recenter = TRUE center new data mean cross-session / cross-subject transfer. Relative (generalized-eigenvalue) whitening. whiten_relative() whitens one covariance reference covariance diagonalizes target — CSP / xDAWN building block — returning filters, variance ratios, patterns. Online updates forgetting. whiten_model_update() gains decay argument exponential -weighting past data track non-stationary drift. Diagonal shrinkage target. whiten_model() (wrappers) gain shrink_target = "diagonal" shrink correlations toward zero preserving per-channel variances. Non-finite handling. whiten_model() (wrappers) gain na_action = "omit" drop trials containing non-finite values. Spatial filters patterns. whitening_patterns() returns whitening filters corresponding forward patterns (Haufe et al., 2014). Richer diagnostics. check_whitening() now also reports cov_dev_frob, logdet, bounded whiteness score.

title: eegwhiten 0.3.0
text: Single eigendecomposition per fit. Covariance-based methods (PCA, SVD, ZCA) longer eigendecompose covariance twice; decomposition computed reused. Analytic shrinkage path tuning. auto_tune_whitening(fast_tune = TRUE) eigendecomposes fold’s covariance reuses across entire lambda / n_comp / var_threshold grid (identity target, covariance-based methods), substantially faster numerically equivalent full refit per candidate.
